blocks.text: Everything is a node. Nodes carry local properties but have no obligation to declare what they are or how they should be used.

sentences.text: Everything is a node.
Nodes carry local properties but have no obligation to declare what they are or how they should be used.

blocks.text: Meaning comes from edges. What a node "is" emerges from the graph relationships that can be traced from it. No edges, no meaning.

sentences.text: Meaning comes from edges.
What a node "is" emerges from the graph relationships that can be traced from it.
No edges, no meaning.

blocks.text: Confidence is proportional to connectivity. The more edges you can trace from a node to well-defined reference points, the more confidently you can characterise that node.

sentences.text: Confidence is proportional to connectivity.
The more edges you can trace from a node to well-defined reference points, the more confidently you can characterise that node.

blocks.text: The system is fractal. Every scope — from the root Lexicon down to a single task — can define its own nodes, edges, types, and vocabulary. The same structural principles apply at every level.

sentences.text: The system is fractal.
Every scope — from the root Lexicon down to a single task — can define its own nodes, edges, types, and vocabulary.
The same structural principles apply at every level.

blocks.text: Anchor nodes enable interoperability without enforcing conformity. The Lexicon provides well-connected reference nodes. Other nodes link to them at whatever granularity makes sense. Partial mapping is normal and expected.

sentences.text: Anchor nodes enable interoperability without enforcing conformity.
The Lexicon provides well-connected reference nodes.
Other nodes link to them at whatever granularity makes sense.
Partial mapping is normal and expected.

blocks.text: Compatibility is computed, not declared. Two nodes are compatible to the degree that their subgraphs overlap when traced toward common reference points. Compatibility is a spectrum, not a boolean.

sentences.text: Compatibility is computed, not declared.
Two nodes are compatible to the degree that their subgraphs overlap when traced toward common reference points.
Compatibility is a spectrum, not a boolean.

blocks.text: Honest uncertainty is the default. The system reports what the graph supports and what it doesn't. It never fills gaps with assumptions.

sentences.text: Honest uncertainty is the default.
The system reports what the graph supports and what it doesn't.
It never fills gaps with assumptions.

blocks.text: Enrichment, not enforcement. When confidence is low, the remedy is adding edges, not adding validation rules. The graph grows; it doesn't constrain.

sentences.text: Enrichment, not enforcement.
When confidence is low, the remedy is adding edges, not adding validation rules.
The graph grows; it doesn't constrain.

blocks.text: Cross-graph edges are first-class. The most powerful connections span graphs: from project issues to Type_Safe definitions, from local types to Lexicon anchors, from Lexicon anchors to schema.org references.

sentences.text: Cross-graph edges are first-class.

blocks.text: No node is aware of how it's used. The information about what a node means and how it participates in workflows is extracted from the surrounding graph structure, not encoded as properties of the node itself.

sentences.text: No node is aware of how it's used.
